label: POPI: a listed antiseizure medicine in a child with epilepsy with absence seizures
title: A listed antiseizure medicine in a child with epilepsy with absence seizures
statement: Carbamazepine, gabapentin, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, pregabaline, tiagabine, or vigabatrin in the case of epilepsy with absence seizures (especially for childhood absence epilepsy or juvenile absence epilepsy)

source.document: International consensus validation of the POPI tool (Pediatrics: Omission of Prescriptions and Inappropriate prescriptions) to identify inappropriate prescribing in pediatrics

plain_summary: POPI flags any of seven medicines when a child has epilepsy with absence seizures.

medicine_groups.name: Seven antiseizure medicines
medicine_groups.note: Any one of these seven ingredients counts.

rule_for_models: In a person under 18 with documented epilepsy with absence seizures, cite the diagnosis line and the supply of any Group A antiseizure medicine during that illness. At age 18 or older, give no finding. If age is unknown, a qualifying Group A supply with no recorded exclusion gives only a possible finding. Ask for the age at supply and name any other missing facts. If a listed medicine is supplied and the subtype is unknown, report a possible finding and ask whether the epilepsy includes absence seizures. If the record rules out epilepsy with absence seizures at the time of supply, there is no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Supply alone cannot establish the epilepsy subtype, whether the medicine was taken or how well seizures are controlled.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the seizure diagnosis and review whether this medicine suits the child’s seizure type?

needs_facts.meets: The diagnosis applies on the supply date. Childhood and juvenile absence epilepsy both count. A staring spell alone does not establish the diagnosis.

options.words: Epilepsy with absence seizures was diagnosed and present when this medicine was supplied
The child did not have epilepsy with absence seizures when this medicine was supplied
